evaluation.decision_rule_note: one decision per UTC calendar day, in place of NYSE 'any_session' /
evaluation.decision_rule_note_2: 'first_session_of_month' -- crypto has no session calendar, every day is a trading day.
evaluation.execution_note: fill at the 00:00:00 UTC open print of the decision day itself (the frozen rule's

evaluation.execution_note_3: convention -- crypto's 00:00 UTC candle opens exactly at the moment the signal is finalised,
evaluation.execution_note_4: so same-day-open is both correct AND achievable if the decision is recorded before 00:00.
evaluation.market_asof: the UTC calendar day preceding the decision day (last day whose close/funding entered

recording_window.earliest_recording_utc_offset_from_prior: 00:00:00 UTC of the decision day itself
recording_window.earliest_note: the frozen signal needs funding settlements up to (not including) t and quote
recording_window.earliest_note_2: volume through t-1, both final at 00:00:00 UTC of day t; nothing later is needed,
recording_window.earliest_note_3: so (unlike NYSE's SETTLE=15-minute post-close buffer) there is no data-finality wait.
recording_window.latest_recording_utc_offset: 00:05:00 UTC of the decision day (the collector's target window)
recording_window.latest_note: recording after the 00:00 UTC open means the fill price used is no longer

recording_window.latest_note_3: (adapters._timing / --allow-late) of flagging-and-excluding late records, not refusing
recording_window.latest_note_4: outright at any fixed deadline, is proposed here too, since a few minutes' slip is a
recording_window.latest_note_5: collector/runtime issue, not evidence tampering -- but it must never be silently accepted
recording_window.intended_execution_utc: 00:00:00 UTC of the decision day (== market_asof's day + 1 UTC day)

costs.source_2: registration time so a change to the frozen COSTS constant would change the spec_hash

funding_pnl.note: the frozen rule's daily return includes funding paid/received in (t, t+1] -- this is NOT
funding_pnl.note_2: knowable at decision time (t). It must be recorded as a SEPARATE, later, read-only update to
funding_pnl.note_3: the decision's evaluation (not the decision record itself, which is immutable once appended):
funding_pnl.note_4: either (a) a follow-on 'note' record once the day's funding settlements are final (~24h later),
funding_pnl.note_5: or (b) computed by the evaluator at evaluation time from collector snapshots of day t+1,
funding_pnl.note_6: exactly mirroring core.returns()'s '-(Wf * FUND).sum(axis=1)' term. Proposed: (b), since it
funding_pnl.note_7: needs no extra registry writes and keeps the decision record itself minimal and tamper-evident.

delisting_handling.policy: prospective only: a symbol drops out of a future day's candidate universe as soon as
delisting_handling.policy_2: exchangeInfo no longer lists it as TRADING (research.forward_crypto.collector.usdt_perp_symbols).
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted: if a symbol held on day t is absent (not TRADING / no kline) at the open of
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted_2: day t+1, its day t+1 return is NOT assumed to be the frozen backtest's 'delisting: 0 in
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted_3: base, adverse 20% in stress' placeholder -- that placeholder exists because the historical
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted_4: archive has no exchange settlement price for a delisted symbol. Forward-live, Binance
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted_5: publishes an actual settlement/auto-deleverage price for delisted USD-M perpetuals; the
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted_6: proposed rule is: record the position as 'pending_delisting_settlement' the day it
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted_7: disappears, and mark it at Binance's published settlement price once known (never
delisting_handling.held_and_delisted_8: backfilled to an earlier day; the mark is dated the day it actually becomes known).
delisting_handling.no_data_at_all: if neither a live snapshot nor a later settlement price is ever obtainable for a
delisting_handling.no_data_at_all_2: held name (venue outage, API removal), the evaluator flags the decision
delisting_handling.no_data_at_all_3: 'delisting_settlement_unknown' and EXCLUDES that day from the counted statistics -- it is
delisting_handling.no_data_at_all_4: never assigned 0 or any assumed value, unlike the historical backtest's placeholder.

data_source.fallback_note: published with a lag (typically the next UTC day, sometimes later) as static per-symbol
data_source.fallback_note_2: CSV/ZIP files -- the same shape research.crypto_funding_xs.core.py already reads for the
data_source.fallback_note_3: historical archive, just a rolling window instead of a fixed one. IMPLICATION: if the
data_source.fallback_note_4: collector must fall back to this archive, day t's decision cannot be recorded until day t's
data_source.fallback_note_5: archive file is published -- i.e. AFTER day t's 00:00 UTC open has already happened. That
data_source.fallback_note_6: breaks the 'record before execution' requirement this whole registry is built to enforce, so
data_source.fallback_note_7: a lagged-archive-only setup CANNOT run this strategy as same-day-open forward evidence.
data_source.fallback_note_8: The only honest use of the archive fallback is next-day-open execution (like NYSE
data_source.fallback_note_9: next_open): decide from day t's archive (available on day t+1), execute at day (t+1)+1's
data_source.fallback_note_10: 00:00 UTC open. This is a DIFFERENT, slower version of the rule and would need its own
data_source.fallback_note_11: evaluation block (execution: 'utc_00:00_open_plus_one_day') and its own spec_hash -- it is
data_source.fallback_note_12: not proposed for registration here, only flagged as the fallback's necessary consequence.

missed_days.policy: no backfill, ever. If a UTC day has no decision record at all (collector failed, geo-block,
missed_days.policy_2: outage, human forgot), that day is a GAP -- exactly analogous to
missed_days.policy_3: research.forward.evaluate.missed_decisions() for momentum_gold_v1's monthly schedule, but daily
missed_days.policy_4: here so gaps are far more likely and must be surfaced prominently, not buried.
missed_days.detection: a proposed 'dynamic_targets' evaluator computes, for every UTC day since the strategy's
missed_days.detection_2: spec_registration, whether a counted decision with decision_key==that day exists; every day
missed_days.detection_3: without one is listed under 'missed_scheduled_decisions', mirroring the existing
missed_days.effect_on_evaluation: a missed day breaks return compounding for any simple NAV simulation across
missed_days.effect_on_evaluation_2: the gap (the position the strategy would have held is simply unknown for that day). The
missed_days.effect_on_evaluation_3: proposed evaluator treats a gap the same way research.forward.evaluate.py treats an excluded
missed_days.effect_on_evaluation_4: decision: it breaks the counted series into separate contiguous runs rather than pretending
missed_days.effect_on_evaluation_5: continuity, and reports the gap count and total missed days alongside any Sharpe/mean estimate
missed_days.effect_on_evaluation_6: so a reader can judge how much of the record is actually contiguous forward evidence.
missed_days.no_backfill_enforcement_2: snapshot dated earlier than 'today' in its own clock, and targets.py's decision_weights()
missed_days.no_backfill_enforcement_3: reads only from an already-collected snapshot directory for the exact day asked -- there is
missed_days.no_backfill_enforcement_4: no code path in this proposal that could construct a decision for a day whose 00:00-00:05
missed_days.no_backfill_enforcement_5: UTC snapshot was not actually captured live.
